research_notes: The safest handoff point is a durable checkpoint boundary after the current smallest safe unit, not an arbitrary wall-clock instant mid-write.
Therefore measured actual elapsed may modestly exceed target even on a correctly executed pass.
That overshoot should be recorded rather than treated as protocol violation.
Systematic large overshoot would indicate units are too coarse for the chosen cap.
Policy-stage task-size controls can reduce that overshoot.
Current generated units are deliberately bounded to keep close boundaries frequent.
